## Why this review exists

The project measures conservation. It does not, on its own, establish what conservation
*means* for translational validity — whether a gene being 84% identical between mouse and
human predicts that a drug acting on it will behave the same way in both. That question
belongs to the literature, and this review is where the answer, or the absence of one, gets
recorded.

A second job: the audit found that **three of the four Daneman source tables were the wrong
tables** and that a paper logged as the macaque dataset contains no macaque samples. Both
were reading errors, not analysis errors. Re-reading the sources carefully, on the record,
is the correction.

## Theme 1 — Defining the blood–brain barrier transcriptome

How the field decided which genes "are" BBB genes, and how much that definition varies
between studies.

### Daneman et al. 2010 {#daneman2010}

> Daneman R, Zhou L, Agalliu D, Cahoy JD, Kaushal A, Barres BA (2010). The mouse
> blood–brain barrier transcriptome: a new resource for understanding the development and
> function of brain endothelial cells. *PLOS ONE* 5(10): e13741.

**Bears on:** [`step1`](audit.qmd) — this is the source of the master gene list.
**Status:** re-read, error found and characterised.

The supplementary tables are not interchangeable, and the pipeline treated them as if they
were. **S3** is a pericyte-specific gene list — `Pdgfrb`, `Kcnj8`, `Vtn`, `Zic1` — not core
BBB genes. **S4** and **S5** are developmentally up- and down-regulated CNS vascular genes,
not the brain-vs-liver and brain-vs-lung endothelial contrasts the pipeline assumed. **S6 is
the BBB-enriched table**: `Slc2a1` (GLUT1), `Slco1a4`, `Slc7a5`, `Ocln`, `Abcb1a`.

The tell was a 1-gene overlap with Munji, which was the correct alarm and the wrong
diagnosis — S3 was not too restrictive, it was a different cell type. Using S6 gives **151
of 411 genes overlapping Munji**, which is what two studies of the same tissue should look
like.

*Annotations: to add.*

### Munji et al. 2019

> Munji RN, et al. (2019). Profiling the mouse brain endothelial transcriptome in health and
> disease. *Nature Neuroscience* 22(11): 1892–1902.

**Bears on:** [`step1`](audit.qmd). **Status:** read, parsed correctly.

518 BBB-enriched mouse genes from sheet `BBB-enriched` of S5. This is the one source table
in step 1 that was read as intended.

*Annotations: to add.*

## Theme 2 — Human brain vascular atlases

Single-cell work that makes it possible to ask whether a mouse-derived gene list holds in
human tissue.

### Wälchli et al. 2024

> Wälchli T, et al. (2024). Single-cell atlas of the human brain vasculature. *Nature* 614:
> 945–954.

**Bears on:** [`step2`, `step4b`](audit.qmd). **Status:** read.

76,125 sorted human brain vascular cells resolving 12 endothelial subtypes. Processed
correctly, then reduced by `step4b` to a single "expressed above zero" test that 88.5% of all
genes pass. **The subtype resolution — the most valuable thing about the dataset — was never
used.** Whether a gene is capillary-specific rather than merely present is the question this
atlas can answer and the pipeline never asked.

*Annotations: to add.*

### Yang et al. 2022

> Yang AC, et al. (2022). A human brain vascular atlas reveals diverse mediators of
> Alzheimer's risk. *Nature* 603: 885–892.

**Bears on:** [`step4b`](audit.qmd). **Status:** re-read needed — only one sheet was used.

The supplementary file has seven sheets: Arterial, Capillary, Venous, SMC, Pericyte,
Fibroblast, Astrocyte. It was read without naming a sheet, so only the first loaded. The
column labelled as human validation actually means "is an arterial marker".

*Annotations: to add.*

### Winkler et al. 2022

> Winkler EA, et al. (2022). A single-cell atlas of the normal and malformed human brain
> vasculature. *Science* 375(6584): eabi7377.

**Bears on:** [`step4b`](audit.qmd). **Status:** read, parsed correctly.

*Annotations: to add.*

## Theme 3 — Translational models and cross-species validity

The literature this project most needs and currently has least of: what is known about
whether sequence conservation predicts pharmacological transferability between species.

### Giger et al. 2010 — withdrawn from the dataset list

> Giger T, et al. (2010). *Evolution of neuronal and endothelial transcriptomes in primates.*

**Bears on:** the macaque arm. **Status:** withdrawn — it is not what it was logged as.

Recorded as the macaque dataset. Its 13 samples are **all human** (`taxid 9606`); the macaque
data in that line of work belongs to Khaitovich et al. under a separate accession that was
never downloaded. It also compares neurons to endothelium rather than brain to peripheral
endothelium, so it is not a BBB gene list for any species.

**Consequence for the project:** there is currently *no* macaque expression evidence. Real
macaque DNA is used throughout steps 5a–5h, but every gene earned its place on the list from
a mouse study. The macaque arm rests on mouse-defined biology, and that assumption has never
been tested.

### Candidate replacement — rhesus macaque brain atlas

> *Science Advances* (2023). Single-nucleus atlas of the rhesus macaque brain, ~1M nuclei
> across 28 regions. Available via CellxGene.

**Status:** identified, not yet obtained. Adding it widens the project's scope and needs
Dr. Clelland's sign-off.

## Theme 4 — Methods for measuring selection

### To add

Background on dN/dS estimation, saturation at long divergence times, and the case for
phylogenetic methods (PAML `codeml`) over pairwise estimates — which is a named
[limitation](results.qmd#limitations) of this project.

## How this project fits in

Once the three breaking defects are fixed, this project contributes a **three-species
coding-sequence comparison of a defined BBB gene set against a tissue control**, with the
mouse–macaque leg included so the triangle closes. What it will not contribute, without new
data, is any statement about macaque BBB *expression*, or about regulatory sequence — the
analysis is coding-sequence only, and regulatory regions are where most cross-species
expression differences are thought to live.
